#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Zip the staged Rainbow_App_Review into its parts, then test extraction against MANIFEST_FILES.tsv."""
import hashlib, json, os, shutil, sys, zipfile

EXP = sys.argv[1]            # .../export (contains Rainbow_App_Review/, records_with_zip.json, zipnames.json)
OUTD = sys.argv[2]           # where the ZIPs go
TEST = sys.argv[3]           # extraction test dir
R = os.path.join(EXP, "Rainbow_App_Review")
recs = json.load(open(os.path.join(EXP, "records_with_zip.json")))
names = json.load(open(os.path.join(EXP, "zipnames.json")))
part_of = {r["path"]: r["zip"] for r in recs}
STORED = (".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".mp4", ".webm", ".apk", ".zip", ".glb", ".spz", ".ply", ".blend", ".webp", ".gz")
os.makedirs(OUTD, exist_ok=True)
groups = {}
for dp, _, fs in os.walk(R):
    for f in fs:
        rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(dp, f), R)
        groups.setdefault(part_of.get(rel, "core"), []).append(rel)   # generated docs (README, MANIFEST, ...) -> core
ONLY = set(os.environ.get("ONLY_PARTS", "").split(",")) - {""}
for part, files in sorted(groups.items()):
    zp = os.path.join(OUTD, names[part])
    if ONLY and part not in ONLY:
        continue
    if os.path.exists(zp):
        os.remove(zp)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# render_slot.sh — run one heavy render (Playwright / SwiftShader / Blender / ffmpeg) while holding one of N machine-wide
# render slots, so the four specialist workers on this 4-CPU container take turns instead of overloading it
# (round 24 ran at load ~30 with repeated Playwright timeouts).
#   usage:  bash /home/user/rainbow-/tools/lead25/render_slot.sh <command> [args...]
#   N = $RENDER_SLOTS (default 2). Waits (polling every 5 s) until a slot is free; prints the wait time on stderr.
#   The exit code is the command's. Slots are flock(1) locks under /tmp, released automatically if the process dies.
#   Status:  bash /home/user/rainbow-/tools/lead25/render_slot.sh --status
N=${RENDER_SLOTS:-2}
if [ "${1:-}" = "--status" ]; then
  for i in $(seq 1 "$N"); do
    if flock -n "/tmp/rainbow-render-slot$i.lock" true 2>/dev/null; then echo "slot $i free"; else echo "slot $i busy"; fi
  done
  exit 0
fi
[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "usage: $0 <command> [args...]" >&2; exit 2; }
t0=$(date +%s)
while true; do
  for i in $(seq 1 "$N"); do
    exec {fd}>"/tmp/rainbow-render-slot$i.lock"
    if flock -n "$fd"; then
      w=$(( $(date +%s) - t0 )); [ "$w" -gt 0 ] && echo "[render_slot] got slot $i after ${w}s" >&2
      nice -n 5 "$@"; rc=$?
      flock -u "$fd"; exec {fd}>&-
      exit $rc
    fi
    exec {fd}>&-
  done
  sleep 5
done

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back unless the tool result says that a notice follows, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling.
